A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FT-Dojo/FT-Agent study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-G are readable, and retained content can be matched across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original fine-tuning experiments across 13 tasks, validation/test results, ablations, and agent decision traces.

after.justification: v2.pdf reports original benchmark experiments, three-run FT-Agent statistics, additional agent and assisted-human comparisons, and a budget-sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: The three-stage FT-Agent procedure, experience and best-configuration tracking, progressive validation, and prompt architecture remain unchanged (Section 3.2; Appendix G). Added planning backbones test the same procedure.

E1.justification: Table 1 and Appendix A retain the same 13 tasks, five domains, and training/evaluation resources. The additional comparisons reuse the existing five-task ablation subset; no new dataset or task scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the focused comparisons with Codex using GPT-5.2, Claude Code using Sonnet-4.6-thinking, and LLM-assisted Manual SFT (Tables 4 and 6). The original base-model, Manual SFT, and OpenHands comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 24-hour OpenHands setting and two open-source planner configurations while retaining the main 12-hour, 2,000-sample protocol. Appendix A.1.1 revises AIME's stated evaluator from MATHVerify to symbolic verification with a GPT-5 fallback; this establishes a reporting revision, without establishing that earlier experiments were rescored.

E4.justification: V2 substantially broadens analyses of comparison fairness and generality: open-source planner sensitivity, the effect of giving manual practitioners LLM assistance, and whether doubling OpenHands' time budget improves AIME performance (Figure 3b; Appendices B.1.3 and B.4). Existing data-scaling, target-size, and failure-case analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 reports point scores without run counts or uncertainty estimates. V2 reports FT-Agent mean and standard deviation over three independent initializations for test and validation results (Tables 2 and 11), explicitly identifies comparison baselines as single-run results, and reports two runs for the extended-budget check.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces FT-Agent point estimates with three-run summaries: Visualization changes from 36.00 to 29.33±6.11 and PI4PC from 44.00 to 49.00±4.36; validation summaries also change. New results include frontier-agent/backbone scores, 20.00% AIME accuracy for assisted Manual SFT, and no improvement from the extended OpenHands budget. These are new or aggregated results, not demonstrated improvements to the method.

T1.justification: The task objective, proposal equation, best-configuration update, and split-allocation formula are retained. Repeating the existing split formula in the main text adds no mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The benchmark and method contributions and the 10-of-13-task claim remain. V2 narrows the novelty assertion to systematic study of an interactive agent task, presents FT-Agent as a strong initial baseline, and removes the conclusion's claim that it uniquely achieves nonzero AIME accuracy.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly states that the constrained Manual SFT comparison is not an expert upper bound and limits model-generalization conclusions to tested 3B/7B settings. It interprets the extended-budget result as evidence of a diagnostic bottleneck. Existing causal-reasoning and planning limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds an implementation repository link and the AIME judge prompt, and clarifies per-method sample budgets, Manual SFT's lack of LLM assistance, and OpenHands' shared wrappers. Appendix A.5 corrects the AIME split prose to 15/15, matching v1's Table 1 rather than establishing a changed split.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Gome, cited as Zhang et al. (2026), and briefly discusses diagnostic reasoning beyond scalar-score tree search. V2 also refines its novelty positioning around systematic interactive fine-tuning evaluation; the existing related-work categories and other cited works remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, conclusion, and selected experimental and baseline paragraphs are rewritten. Focused-comparison and evaluator subsections and a conflict-of-interest disclosure are added, while the overall section order and most method and appendix prose are preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds comparison Tables 4 and 6, redraws Figure 3 with additional planner bars and revised labels, and reformats the main and validation tables to accommodate uncertainty reporting. Other figures and appendix tables are largely retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind v1's broad superiority claims through FT-Agent uncertainty reporting, frontier-agent and assisted-human comparisons, and budget checks, while narrowing conclusions accordingly. Evaluator and baseline clarifications also improve transparency. Single-run comparators and older point estimates retained in Appendix C remain limitations, but the gains substantially improve the evaluation's credibility.
